source_row.item_data_json: {"options":{"A":"Use the results only to identify individual staff for discipline without unit-level improvement feedback.","B":"Replace infection-prevention education with audit scores because measurement alone changes practice.","C":"Use the results to identify adherence gaps and provide regular feedback that supports improvement.","D":"Collect compliance data for reporting purposes without discussing findings or changing practice."}}
source_row.rationale: CDC recommends monitoring adherence to infection-prevention practices and providing prompt, regular feedback so gaps and outcomes can be improved. Option C is correct. Monitoring is not intended to replace education, function only as punishment, or remain disconnected from improvement.
source_row.source_detail: Performance Monitoring and Feedback: identify and monitor adherence to infection-prevention practices, use standardized tools when available, and provide prompt, regular feedback on adherence and related outcomes. Current CDC Core Practices live-rechecked 2026-08-15. NCSBN first-check: Client Needs — Safe and Effective Care Environment — Safety and Infection Prevention and Control: transmission precautions, PPE, device/environmental safety, asepsis, identification and infection-prevention activities as applicable. 2026 NCLEX-RN Test Plan; effective 2026-04-01 through 2029-03-31; currentness rechecked 2026-08-15.
